prompt:
Character turnaround sheet of the EXACT character in the reference image: a cute chibi human warrior with a very big head, shoulder-length wavy dark brown hair, brown eyes, light stubble, warm tan skin, steel plate armor with copper trim and rivets, layered pauldrons, a brown leather belt with a square bronze buckle, and a short plate skirt. Three views side by side in ONE row on a flat solid magenta (#FF00FF) background, all at the SAME scale and standing on the SAME baseline, with wide empty magenta gaps between them:
LEFT - the front view, exactly as in the reference image.
MIDDLE - an exact side profile, the whole body turned 90 degrees so he faces the RIGHT edge of the picture; one eye, the nose and the chin in profile, the hair falling behind the ear, the near arm hanging at his side with the fist at the same height as in the front view.
RIGHT - the back view seen straight from behind: the back of the hair, the back plate, the backs of the pauldrons, the belt going round, both fists at his sides.
Keep the proportions identical in all three: the head is exactly the same size, and the top of the head, the chin, the shoulders, the belt and the lower hem of the armor skirt are at exactly the same heights in every view. Same painted chibi game-art style, same colours, same thick dark outline as the reference. The hands are empty fists - no weapon, no shield. Like the reference, each figure ends at the hem of the armor skirt: no legs and no feet below it. No shadow, no floor, no text, no labels, no frame.
cut: One scale for all three views: the sheet's front is made as tall as the original sprite (800 px). Magenta keyed by its excess min(R,B)-G (this palette has no colour near it, so enclosed gaps go too), edge colours unmixed from the magenta, any purple cast left (the plate reflects the background) taken off so min(R,B) never stands more than 10 above G - as in the original - and the edge tightened to the original's crispness. Each view stands on the bottom edge of an 800 px canvas, cropped tight left and right, so drawn at the front's height it keeps its true size.
